report.summary: Four tests failed, and they come from two product bugs in app/main.py. `list_books` returns every user's books, and the year check accepts next year. Fix both in the app. The tests are correct and need no changes.

causes.title: Book listing ignores the owner, so users see each other's books
causes.explanation: `list_books` takes `user_id` but never uses it in the query. It returns all users' books from both the API and the UI bookshelf. This breaks the privacy test. It also explains why a newly registered user does not see the empty bookshelf, because other users' books are shown. I did not read the UI page object or template, so that link is inferred.
evidence: app/main.py:149: conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()  (no WHERE owner_id = ?)
causes.suggested_fix: Change the query to `SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id` and pass `(user_id,)`. Also add `AND owner_id = ?` to the UPDATE and DELETE statements as defence in depth.

causes.title: Year validation accepts next year, although the error message says the maximum is this year
causes.explanation: `validate_book` allows years up to `this_year + 1`, but the error message says "between 1 and {this_year}" and `test_current_year_is_accepted` treats this year as the upper bound. Next year is therefore accepted, giving 201 on the API and no error in the UI.
evidence: app/main.py:84: f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}"
causes.suggested_fix: Change the check to `1 <= book.year <= this_year`.
